rows.jp: さてと。
rows.en: Now, then.

ghs.en: Well then now.

rows.jp: 部活の方は、他の人々に任せて、と。
rows.en: I'll leave the club work to the others.

ghs.en: Club activities are left in the hands of others, so,

rows.jp: 冬子を拾ってきますか。
rows.en: Time to go pick up Touko.

ghs.en: shall I not go recover Touko?
ghs.assessment: Taichi proposes going to pick Touko up. 'Recover Touko' treats her as a lost object or a rescue target.

highlights.text: shall I not go recover Touko?

rows.jp: 車で行こう。
rows.en: I'll drive.

ghs.en: I'll go by car.

rows.jp: 職員室から鍵をあさり、合う車を探す。
rows.en: I rummage through the keys in the staff room, looking for a car one of them fits.

ghs.en: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese gives a single present narrative sequence of rummaging for keys and finding the matching car. The English arbitrarily mixes past and present.

highlights.text: I scrounged a key from the staff room, and I now search for the matching car.

rows.en: “Whoa……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ouch..."

rows.jp: 駐車場は惨劇になっていた。
rows.en: The parking lot is a scene of carnage.

ghs.en: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.
ghs.assessment: The parking lot is described metaphorically as a scene of disaster. 'A tragedy had taken place' asserts an actual tragic event.

highlights.text: A tragedy had taken place in the parking area.

rows.jp: まるで暴走車が、当て逃げを繰り返したみたいに。
rows.en: As though a runaway car had careened through, committing hit-and-run after hit-and-run.

ghs.en: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.
ghs.assessment: The comparison is to a runaway or rampaging car repeatedly striking vehicles and fleeing. The English substitutes a 'rampant driver' and the formal criminal phrase 'performed hit-and-runs.'

highlights.text: It's as if a rampant driver had performed repeated hit-and-runs, over and over.

rows.jp: 「全部凹んでる……」
rows.en: “They're all dented……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "They're all dented..."

rows.jp: こっちはバンパーがもげてる。
rows.en: This one's bumper has been torn off.

ghs.en: Here we have a torn-off bumper,

rows.jp: 木が折れてる。
rows.en: A tree has been snapped.

ghs.en: there a tree was splintered,

rows.jp: フロントに放射状にヒビが。
rows.en: One windshield is cracked in a radial pattern.

ghs.en: cracks in that front radiator...
ghs.assessment: フロント here refers to the front glass or windshield bearing radiating cracks. A radiator does not take radial visible cracking in the described list, and the Japanese does not name one.

highlights.text: cracks in that front radiator...

rows.jp: 「……友貴先生……」
rows.en: “……Professor Tomoki……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...Tomoki-sensei..."

rows.jp: 神々しいまでに運転の才能がない友貴だった。
rows.en: Tomoki's lack of driving talent approached the divine.

ghs.en: Tomoki had a lack of driving talent that reached the divine.

rows.jp: 「やっぱ素人にミッションは無理か、ククク」
rows.en: “A manual transmission really is too much for an amateur. Heh heh.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"
ghs.assessment: ミッション is Japanese automotive shorthand for a manual transmission, with a joke about an amateur handling it. Leaving it as English 'mission' loses the automotive meaning.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Truly, amateurs on that 'mission aren't gonna make it, keh keh keh!"

rows.jp: そこへ行くと俺なんか、ちゃんと乗り方知ってるもんね。
rows.en: Whereas I know perfectly well how to drive one.

ghs.en: When it comes to myself, however, I really know how to ride these things.

rows.jp: 人間としての格の違いってやつか。
rows.en: It is what you might call the difference in our rank as human beings.

ghs.en: Is it just the difference in our levels of humanity?

rows.jp: キーの合った車に乗り込む。
rows.en: I climb into the car whose key fits.

ghs.en: I get on the car that fits the key.
ghs.assessment: One gets into a car, not 'on the car.'

highlights.text: I get on the car that fits the key.

rows.jp: 男だから当然ミッションだ。
rows.en: I'm a man, so naturally it has a manual transmission.

ghs.en: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that because he is a man, naturally the car is a manual transmission. The English uses the unrelated word 'mission' and leaves the sentence dangling into the punch line.

highlights.text: I am a man, therefore the 'mission, naturally,

rows.jp: オートマ。
rows.en: An automatic.

ghs.en: is automatic.

rows.jp: 女子供の乗り物だな。
rows.en: A vehicle for women and children.

ghs.en: It's a vehicle for women and children, they say.

rows.jp: 「ケッ、見せてやるぜよ！」
rows.en: “Hah! I'll show you, by thunder!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Pah, I'm gonna show you now!"

rows.jp: 荒々しい俺だった。
rows.en: I am a rough customer.

ghs.en: I was rough and wild.

rows.jp: ちょっと龍馬入ってる。
rows.en: A little Sakamoto Ryōma had slipped into my diction.

ghs.en: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.
ghs.assessment: 龍馬 refers to Ryoma and explains Taichi's imitation of the distinctive ぜよ speech. The English translates the name's characters as a generic 'war horse' and invents a battle description.

highlights.text: There's also a bit of the war horse, gallant in the face of battle.

rows.jp: 半クラッチから見事にアクセルを繋いだ。
rows.en: I bring the clutch to the bite point and feed in the gas with consummate skill.

ghs.en: I magnificently accelerate from a half-clutch position.

rows.jp: いかん、目の前の車にぶつけてしまった。
rows.en: Oh no. I hit the car in front of me.

ghs.en: Dammit, I just bumped into that car in front of me!

rows.jp: シートベルトしててよかった。
rows.en: Good thing I put on my seat belt.

ghs.en: Good thing I fastened my seatbelt.

rows.jp: とりあえず後退しよう。
rows.en: For now, I'll reverse.

ghs.en: For now let's back out.

rows.jp: 「バック石松、バック石松っと……」
rows.en: “Guts Ishimatsu? No—Back Ishimatsu. Back, back……”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Back Isshimatsu, Back Isshimatsu, and..."

rows.jp: タイヤ止めを乗り越えて背後の樹木をへし折ってしまったぞ。
rows.en: I roll over the wheel stop and snap the tree behind me.

ghs.en: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.
ghs.assessment: The car crosses the wheel stop and snaps the tree behind it. The English changes the tree into shrubbery and merely says that the car breaks into it.

highlights.text: Overcoming the tire stops I break into the shrubbery on the back.

rows.jp: 「バッドだぜ～」
rows.en: “Baaad, man.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Baddo this is～"

rows.jp: こんなミス、百万回に一度もない。超レアイベントだ。
rows.en: A mistake like this would not happen once in a million tries. An ultra-rare event.

ghs.en: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that this mistake would not happen even once in a million times and calls it hyper-rare. 'Isn't a one in a million' normally denies that it is rare and contradicts the next sentence.

highlights.text: This kind of mistake isn't a one in a million. A Hyper Rare Event.

rows.jp: リトライ。
rows.en: Retry.

ghs.en: Reee-try.

rows.jp: しまった、ギアがバックのままだった。
rows.en: Damn it. The gear was still in reverse.

ghs.en: Dammit, it was still in reverse gear.

rows.jp: 百万分の一に百万分の一をかけると……いくつだ。
rows.en: A one-in-a-million chance times another one-in-a-million chance…… What does that make?

ghs.en: Multiply one in a million by one in a million... how much's even that.

rows.jp: まあいい。
rows.en: Well, never mind.

ghs.en: Ah, who cares.

rows.jp: きらめくほどに俺は奇跡的なのだ。
rows.en: I was miraculous enough to sparkle.

ghs.en: I'm so miraculous I could just sparkle.

rows.jp: 高そうな車なのに……すまん、今は亡き榊原教諭。
rows.en: And it looks so expensive…… Sorry, the late Mr. Sakakibara.

ghs.en: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.
ghs.assessment: 今は亡き is the conventional 'late' for a deceased person, and 教諭 is a teacher. 'Currently-Deceased Professor' is an unnatural, comic bureaucratic construction not present in the Japanese.

highlights.text: And that car even looks so expensive... sorry, Currently-Deceased Professor Sakakibara.

rows.jp: 前に出る。
rows.en: I move forward.

ghs.en: I head forwards.

rows.jp: おっとっと、サイドブレーキ入れたままだった。
rows.en: Whoops. I left the parking brake on.

ghs.en: Whoa, whoa, woah the handbrake was still engaged.

rows.jp: 戻す。
rows.en: I release it.

ghs.en: Disengage.

rows.jp: がくん、と車が急加速する。
rows.en: The car lurches into sudden acceleration.

ghs.en: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.
ghs.assessment: がくん describes the car lurching as it accelerates. 'Boom' introduces an explosive sound.

highlights.text: Boom, the car accelerates suddenly.

rows.jp: 横一列に並んでいた車の鼻先をかすめながら、バンパーをもぎっていく。
rows.en: It clips the noses of the cars parked in a row and tears off their bumpers as it goes.

ghs.en: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.
ghs.assessment: The car clips the noses of vehicles lined in a single row and tears off their bumpers as it goes. The English changes the row to plural rows and leaves a single bumper without a clear owner.

highlights.text: Grazing the noses of the cars parked in the rows, and ripping off the bumper.

rows.jp: かなり効率よく破壊してしまったぞ。
rows.en: I have destroyed them with remarkable efficiency.

ghs.en: I'm pretty efficient at destruction dammit.

rows.jp: やべー、校長のフェラーリもひどいことに。
rows.en: Oh, crap. The principal's Ferrari is in terrible shape too.

ghs.en: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.
ghs.assessment: The narrator observes that the principal's Ferrari is now in terrible condition too. The English explicitly makes him the agent and describes an intentionally 'nasty' act.

highlights.text: No waaay, I did something really nasty to the headmaster's Ferrari.

ghs.en: Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: ま、いっか。こんな危険な学校でフェラる方が悪い。
rows.en: Oh well. Anyone who Ferraris at a dangerous school like this has only himself to blame.

ghs.en: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese pun blames the person who brings or drives a Ferrari at such a dangerous school. The English turns the pun into an unrelated claim that sexual activity at school is improper.

highlights.text: Ah, who cares. F'ing in this dangerous school is improper.

rows.jp: ※フェラる＝太一語。二つの意味が。①フェラーリのオーナーになること。②（全略）
rows.en: ※To Ferrari—Taichi-speak, with two meanings: (1) to own a Ferrari; (2) [entirely omitted].

rows.jp: ゆっくりと前進。右折。
rows.en: I advance slowly. Right turn.

ghs.en: Slow forwards. Turn right.

rows.jp: 「いいぞ」
rows.en: “Good.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Awesome."

rows.jp: エンストした。
rows.en: The engine stalls.

ghs.en: Engine stalled.
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: リスタート。
rows.en: Restart.

ghs.en: Start again.

rows.jp: バックした。
rows.en: I reverse.

ghs.en: Reverse.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: つくづく思うけど、シートベルトって必須だよな。
rows.en: The thought keeps occurring to me: seat belts really are indispensable.

ghs.en: But I think that, through and through, seatbelts really are indispensable.

rows.jp: 「くじけずＧＯ！」
rows.en: “Undaunted—go!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Undauntedly GO!"
ghs.assessment: くじけずＧＯ is an exhortation not to give up and to go. 'Undauntedly GO' uses an unnatural adverb.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Undauntedly GO!"

rows.jp: 車が動かなくなった。
rows.en: The car won't move anymore.

ghs.en: The car did not move anymore.

rows.jp: 「……うーむ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hm-hmmm."

rows.jp: バイオリズムが不調らしい。
rows.en: My biorhythms must be off.

ghs.en: My biorhythms seem to be off today.

rows.jp: 「しかし日本車のもろいことよ」
rows.en: “Japanese cars are awfully fragile.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But damn, Japanese cars are so fragile!"

rows.jp: こんな車で西部の警察に配属されることなど、夢のまた夢。
rows.en: With a car like this, being assigned to the Western Police would remain a dream within a dream.

ghs.en: The idea that this car would ever be deployed to the police in the West is but dream within dream.

rows.jp: せいぜいが放水車で破壊されるが関の山。
rows.en: At best, it would only be wrecked by a water-cannon truck.

ghs.en: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.
ghs.assessment: The car's best prospect is to end up destroyed by a water-cannon truck. 'Water cannon fire engines' conflates vehicle types and changes the singular car into plural 'they.'

highlights.text: The best they could do is get wrecked by water cannon fire engines, and no more.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんが窓を叩いていた。
rows.en: Yoko is tapping on the window.

ghs.en: Youko-chan knocked on the window.

rows.en: “……What?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...what?"

rows.jp: 窓をあけて。
rows.en: I roll it down.

ghs.en: I open the window.

rows.jp: 「おりて」
rows.en: “Get out.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Get out."

rows.jp: おりる。
rows.en: I get out.

ghs.en: I get out.

rows.jp: 「待ってて」
rows.en: “Wait here.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Wait here."

rows.en: “……Yeah.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...'k."

rows.jp: 地面に『の』の字を書きながら待っていると、奥からするすると車が走ってきた。
rows.en: I wait, tracing sulky little spirals on the ground, until a car glides out from the back.

ghs.en: I pass the time by embarrassedly spiraling my finger in the ground in the shape of the 'no' hiragana, until a car came smoothly riding out from the back.
ghs.assessment: Drawing の on the ground conventionally depicts dejection or sulking in this context. The English labels the gesture embarrassment and adds a spiraling motion not stated by the source.

highlights.text: I pass the time by embarrassedly spiraling my finger in the ground in the shape of the 'no' hiragana, until a car came smoothly riding out from the back.

rows.jp: 淀みのない運転で、目の前に停車。
rows.en: The car glides to a stop in front of me.

ghs.en: Driving without hesitation, it stops right in front of me.
ghs.assessment: Youko drives smoothly and stops before Taichi. 'Driving without hesitation, it stops' attaches the human action of driving to the car.

highlights.text: Driving without hesitation, it stops right in front of me.

rows.jp: 「乗って」
rows.en: “Get in.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Get on."
ghs.assessment: The command for entering a car is 'Get in,' not 'Get on.'

highlights.text: Youko: "Get on."

rows.jp: 助手席に乗る。
rows.en: I get into the passenger seat.

ghs.en: I get in the passenger's seat.

rows.jp: 「どこに行きたいの？」
rows.en: “Where do you want to go?”

ghs.en: Youko: "Where do you want to go?"

rows.jp: 「……桐原城ですお世話になります」
rows.en: “……Kirihara Castle. Thank you for the ride.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose."
ghs.assessment: Taichi gives the destination, Kirihara Castle, and courteously thanks her for the ride. 'Castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose' reverses the name and turns the thanks into a request.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...castle Kirihara, if I may graciously impose."

rows.jp: 連れて行ってもらった。
rows.en: She takes me there.

ghs.en: I was being taken there.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that she took him there. 'I was being taken' uses an incomplete progressive passive and suppresses the driver.

highlights.text: I was being taken there.

rows.jp: 悲しい気持ちでいっぱいになった。
rows.en: I am filled with sadness.

ghs.en: And so it was that I became filled with sad feelings.
